reason: The recycling cells are shown surrounding worn red cells, so this looks like the first step toward recovering their iron.
expectation: The worn cells will be broken down and their iron recovered for reuse.

effect: The iron is recovered and carried in blood, ready to be reused in marrow.
reaction: It makes sense that the recycling cells remain intact while the old cells are broken down.
reason: The marrow makes developing blood cells and already has the other nutrients, so the recovered iron belongs there.

choice.combine: Iron recovered from old blood cells

expectation: The marrow will use the recovered iron to make new red blood cells.

effect: The recovered iron is now in the oxygen-carrying protein of new red cells; the skin-cell goal remains.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the iron reused while the marrow's stem cells remain.
reason: The picture shows the supplied materials moving to the dividing skin cells for growth.

choice.combine: Dividing cells at the skin's base
choice.with: Water, glucose and cell building materials

expectation: The skin cells will use the materials to grow replacements while the base population remains.

effect: The new skin cells appear above the intact base population while old surface cells shed, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: It was satisfying to see renewal without the skin losing its continuous covering.

mostWorthwhile.text: Reusing recovered iron in marrow was most worthwhile: it connected old red cells to the oxygen-carrying protein in new ones.

leastWorthwhile.text: The skin-cell combination was clear but predictable from the picture, so it involved little decision-making.

surprise.text: I hadn't expected the recovered iron to travel in blood attached to proteins rather than as visible fragments.

arbitrary.text: None felt arbitrary; the pictures explained why each pairing belonged together.

continue.text: I would probably continue if another chapter offered a new connection to figure out. This chapter made renewal understandable, though its pairings were quite direct.
